summary:
DD-Channel/ra2-web exists, but it is not an independent project. It is an untouched GitHub fork of huangkaoya/ts-redalert2 (also reachable as huangkaoya/redalert2). The GitHub API reports "fork":true with parent "huangkaoya/ts-redalert2". main (786800b, 2025-09-14) is identical to an upstream commit, and upstream main is now 97 commits ahead (status "ahead", behind_by 0). No DD-Channel member has committed to main. The only other branch, cyhan/dev, holds 13 small type-fix commits by "Cyhan" from 2025-06/07. DD-Channel is an organization that bookmark-forks many unrelated repos (stable-diffusion-webui, StarRailCopilot, OpenSAGE and others).

The code is a reconstruction of the proprietary, closed-source Chrono Divide web client. The fork's own README says so. The previous README version (commit cc0e14c, 2025-08-07) said it outright: "这是基于 AI 对《时空分裂（chronodivide）》客户端的反编译" ("based on AI decompilation of the Chrono Divide client"). On 2026-09-03 the upstream author replaced GPL-3.0 with a notice that Chrono Divide-derived material "is not licensed under GPL-3.0 or any other open-source license". The code itself confirms this. There is leftover minified SystemJS module code, variables with single-letter minified names, comments quoting "Original JS: var r = ...", and src/test/Original*.js files marked "直接从原项目转换" ("converted directly from the original project"). The repo also ships Chrono Divide's ra2cd.mix, EA's rules.ini/art.ini (inside public/ini.mix), Chrono Divide's locale strings, and config pointing at Chrono Divide servers and a third-party "full-pack.7z" download of the game files.

Functionally, this snapshot offers only skirmish, against a DummyBot that deploys its MCV and then does nothing. There is no campaign, no multiplayer netcode (the turn manager is a placeholder), no Yuri's Revenge gameplay, no save/load and no map editor. `npm run build` fails at the tsc step. `vite build` alone succeeds in 2.4s.

The renderer design is a reasonable fit for an HD remaster: Three.js r177 on WebGL2, a fixed-angle orthographic camera, palette-lookup shaders, and voxels built as real 3D meshes. That does not make up for the legal problem. It is not usable as a base, and even for reference the upstream repo is strictly newer.
license_evidence:
VERIFIED, from the clone and the GitHub API:
(1) The fork's LICENSE file is the full GNU GPL v3 text (35,149 bytes), and `gh api repos/DD-Channel/ra2-web` reports license spdx_id "GPL-3.0".
(2) package.json has no "license" field and sets "private": true.
(3) The README contradicts the GPL grant. It says "all rights to the project (including profit rights) belong to the owner of Chronodivide", that commercial use without permission is "strictly prohibited", and that "the owner of Chronodivide has never open-sourced the game client code in any form". Commercial use is to be "deemed as infringement against Alexandru Ciucă". The README also still carries a separate "本项目基于GNU General Public License v3.0（GPL-3.0）许可证开源" (GPL-3.0) section.
(4) The upstream parent huangkaoya/ts-redalert2 replaced its GPL LICENSE in commit 898d891 (2026-09-03, "Revise LICENSE to reflect copyright holder's terms"). The new LICENSE says: "This repository contains code reconstructed from the Chrono Divide client. The Chrono Divide copyright holder has not licensed Chrono Divide-derived material contained in this repository. Such material is not licensed under GPL-3.0 or any other open-source license." The GitHub API now reports upstream license spdx_id "NOASSERTION".
(5) The fork predates that change, so it still displays the GPL text the upstream author has since disclaimed.

CONCLUSION (inference, not legal advice): the GPL-3.0 grant on this fork is not credible. The licensor states the rights belong to a third party who never licensed them. For practical purposes the code is proprietary Chrono Divide material with no license to build on. On top of that, EA's copyrighted rules.ini/art.ini/ai.ini/sound.ini/eva.ini are bundled in public/ini.mix, and Chrono Divide's own ra2cd.mix is bundled in public/res.
provenance: A GitHub fork of huangkaoya/ts-redalert2 with no changes of its own on main. The code is a TypeScript reconstruction, largely AI-assisted deobfuscation, of the proprietary, never-open-sourced Chrono Divide client (game.chronodivide.com), by way of its Chinese-localized "RA2WEB" deployment.

VERIFIED:

- Authorship: `git shortlog --all` shows huangkaoya (110 commits) and Cyhan (13, cyhan/dev only). There are no DD-Channel commits. The contributors API lists only huangkaoya.
- Admissions in the README: cc0e14c (2025-08-07) said "这是基于 AI 对《时空分裂（chronodivide）》客户端的反编译（game.chronodivide.com）". 7b1d0f3 (2025-09-07) softened this to "developed based on the analysis of the Chinese version RA2WEB of the Chronodivide client". The contribution guide still says "迁移模块 - 将JavaScript模块转换为TypeScript" ("migrate modules: convert JavaScript modules to TypeScript").
- Bulk import: the largest commit is bd49b31 (2025-06-01, "feat: core game engine"), +41,019 lines across 452 files in one commit. Others: 572ee5a +26,218 lines/194 files; 845cd06 +19,942 lines/138 files.
- Leftover minified original: src/engine/renderable/entity/TargetLines.ts line 297 contains a raw `System.register("engine/renderable/entity/TargetLines", [...], function (e, t) { "use strict"; var h, u, d, i; ... execute: function () { e("TargetLines", (i = class { constructor(e, t, i, r, s) {...`. This is Chrono Divide's SystemJS bundle format with minified names. src/gui/component/Dialog.tsx:79 has the comment "based on original System.register".
- Minified identifiers in live code: VxlGeometryCulledBuilder.ts uses variables a, n, t, o, l, c, h, u, d, g, p, m, f, y, T, E, v, b, S, w, C.
- Comments: TileSetEntry.ts:45 "Original JS: var r = this.files[t(0, this.files.length - 1)];". Config.ts:63 "Original code `for (var [s, a] of r.entries)`". WolConnection.ts "Copied from the original project (see network/WolConnection.js)". src/test/OriginalBlowfish.js, OriginalMixEntry.js and others are headed "原始…实现，直接从原项目转换" ("original ... implementation, converted directly from the original project"). 82 comments reference "original code/project".
- Chrono Divide artifacts: public/config.ini points mapsBaseUrl/modsBaseUrl at gameres.chronodivide.com, and the CORS proxy at game.chronodivide.com. public/servers.ini lists wss://wol-eu1.chronodivide.com and wol-sea1. public/res/locale/en-US.json contains "Thank you for playing Chrono Divide!". GameLoader.ts imports '@chronodivide/sp-bots' via SystemJS. public/res/ra2cd.mix contains rulescd.ini headed "# Chrono Divide rules override".
- The distinctive Chrono Divide design (Symbol-keyed trait notification interfaces such as `[NotifySpawn.onSpawn]`, WOL/IRC lobby classes, a ladder service) is reproduced throughout.

Similarity to other candidates: OpenRA2/RA2Web is also a GitHub fork of huangkaoya/ts-redalert2, so it shares the same lineage. ra2-games/ra2 (created 2026-09-12, not a fork) shares only 7 of 1,208 file paths with this repo, so it is structurally different (TaiYouWeb/ra2 is a fork of it). Its provenance was not checked here.

External, per third-party listings: several GitHub projects describe Chrono Divide's engine as "proprietary, used with the author's permission, non-commercial only" (https://github.com/ammaarreshi/RedAlert2-Mac-iOS-iPad). chronodivide.com calls itself "a non-profit fan project" and publishes no license for its client (https://chronodivide.com/).
tech_stack:
VERIFIED from package.json and the lockfile install: React ^18.2 + react-dom (UI mixed with a custom JSX renderer), TypeScript ^5.3.3 with "strict": false and "noImplicitAny": false, Vite 5.4.19 (+ @vitejs/plugin-react), and three ^0.177.0 (0.177.0 installed; @types/three 0.176).

Other runtime dependencies: @brakebein/threeoctree (spatial culling), shader-particle-engine (needs a global THREE, set in src/setupThreeGlobal.ts), three.meshline, @ffmpeg/ffmpeg (listed but barely used), 7z-wasm (archive import), @ra2web/pcxfile, @ra2web/wavefile, @puzzl/core, mersenne-twister, js-logger, stats.js, and liang-barsky. Also bundled: public/libs/fsalib.min.js (File System Access polyfill), lzo1x.js, 7zz.wasm, and a third-party file-explorer.js.

Size: 1,178 source files, about 127k lines of TS/TSX (game ~46k, gui ~34k, engine ~31k, data ~7k). There are 4,635 `any` usages. npm is the package manager (package-lock.json).
renderer_architecture:
VERIFIED in code:

Renderer: src/engine/gfx/Renderer.ts creates a single THREE.WebGLRenderer (three r177, so WebGL2 only) with powerPreference 'high-performance', preserveDrawingBuffer, shadowMap.enabled, NoToneMapping and outputColorSpace = LinearSRGBColorSpace ("to match the original project"). Scenes (WorldScene plus UiScene) are rendered sequentially with manual viewport and depth clears. There is no render target and no post-processing chain, and no WebGPU. supportsInstancing() checks the WebGL1 'ANGLE_instanced_arrays' extension, which is stale under WebGL2.

Camera: WorldScene.createCamera builds a THREE.OrthographicCamera with rotation order 'YXZ' and fixed iso angles (Coords.COS_ISO_CAMERA_BETA / ISO_WORLD_SCALE). This gives true 2.5D: the world is 3D, viewed through a fixed orthographic isometric camera. CameraPan and CameraZoom are separate modules.

Parsing (src/data): MixFile/MixEntry (with Blowfish-encrypted headers, via encoding/), IdxFile/AudioBagFile, ShpFile/ShpImage (Format80/Format5 decoders), VxlFile plus vxl/ and HvaFile plus hva/, TmpFile/TmpImage, Palette.ts (256 colors with remap(baseColor) for house colors from REMAP_START_IDX), PcxFile, CsfFile, IniFile/IniParser, MapFile/MapObjects plus map/ (tags, triggers, lighting), and WavFile/Mp3File. The virtual file system (src/data/vfs) layers the MIX archives on top of browser storage.

SHP to texture: ShpBuilder/ShpTextureAtlas/BatchShpBuilder pack SHP frames into RGBA textures whose channel holds a palette index, not a color. PaletteBasicMaterial (it extends MeshBasicMaterial) plus paletteShaderLib.ts do the color lookup. The fragment shader reads the index from texelColor.a (or .r when USE_RED_INDEX is set) and samples a palette LUT texture: `texture2D(palette, vec2(index, (paletteOffset+0.5)/paletteCount))`. TextureUtils.textureFromPalettes stacks several palettes as rows, and per-instance or per-vertex palette offsets select the house-color remap row. Sprites are camera-facing quads with nearest filtering. SpriteUtils handles offsets and anchors.

TMP terrain: MapTileLayer draws every TmpImage through TmpDrawable into one index-texture TextureAtlas, merges the tile quads into a BufferGeometry, and renders them with PaletteBasicMaterial and the iso palette. Per-tile lighting is a vertexColorMult attribute (USE_VERTEX_COLOR_MULT). Shroud is MapShroudLayer; sprite batching is MapSpriteBatchLayer.

VXL/HVA: VxlBuilderFactory → VxlBatchedBuilder / VxlNonBatchedBuilder → VxlGeometryPool → VxlGeometryMonotoneBuilder, which greedy-meshes the voxels into a real THREE.BufferGeometry. Vertex color .r holds the palette index, and voxel normals come from the VXL normal table. The result is lit with PaletteLambertMaterial or PalettePhongMaterial (these extend the Three built-ins with the palette chunks plus an extraLight term). Geometry is cached in browser storage by VxlGeometryCache/BufferGeometrySerializer. HVA drives the section matrices. Voxels are therefore true real-time 3D meshes, not pre-rendered sprites. The alternative Culled and Naive builders still call THREE.BoxBufferGeometry (removed in modern Three) and are dead code.

Lighting: one THREE.AmbientLight plus one DirectionalLight with an optional shadow map (1024 × quality multiplier, orthographic shadow camera). Map lighting comes from Lighting.ts/MapLighting (ambient, per-tile lights) and LightingDirector with LightningStormFx and NukeLightingFx. Sprites are unlit apart from an additive extraLight tint.

FX: src/engine/renderable/fx (LaserFx, TeslaFx, RadBeamFx, SparkFx, TrailerSmokeFx via shader-particle-engine, and others) plus handlers (WarheadDetonateFxHandler, SuperWeaponFxHandler, ChronoFxHandler, and others). Explosions are the original SHP animations (Anim/TransientAnim). TeslaFx calls `new THREE.LightningStrike`, which is not exported by three core. Vite warns about this, and it is likely a runtime TypeError when a Tesla weapon fires (inference).

Sim/render split: src/game (World, Game, GameObject plus about 61 traits, orders, tasks, triggers, rules) is mostly separate from src/engine/renderable (RenderableFactory, entity/*, plugins). Only game/math wraps Three math types, although 86 game files import from engine/.

Netcode: GameTurnManager.ts is a stub ("No-op: real implementation handled in networked managers in the original project"). There is no lockstep implementation. src/network is only about 1k lines (WOL/IRC stubs, game-option parsers, ladder HTTP).

Audio: src/engine/sound (Web Audio: AudioSystem, Mixer, Music, Eva, WorldSound, SoundSpecs), reading audio.bag/idx.

Video: only the menu background video, played as .webm/.mp4. The comments say "Found .bik file but cannot play directly"; there is no Bink decoder and no in-game FMV system.

build_result:
Tested on macOS with Node v26.0.0 and npm 11.12.1.

`npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`: OK, 94 packages in 6s.

`npm run build` (= `tsc && vite build`): FAILED at tsc with exit 2 after about 1.3s:
  src/engine/renderable/entity/TargetLines.ts(566,5): error TS1109: Expression expected.
  src/engine/renderable/entity/TargetLines.ts(567,3): error TS1005: '}' expected.
The cause is raw SystemJS/minified code pasted at line 297 of that file. The file is not imported anywhere, so it is dead code.

With that one file excluded (temporary tsconfig, since removed), `tsc --noEmit` reports 2,319 errors. By code: 769 TS6133 (unused), 674 TS2339 (property does not exist), 211 TS2345, 135 TS2341, 87 TS6138, 49 TS2322, 46 TS2554, 46 TS2304 (cannot find name, e.g. 'THREE', 'TheaterSettings'), and 31 TS2307 (missing modules such as '@/engine/gfx/Camera', '@/network/WolError', '@/game/GameObject'). The worst files are MoveTask.ts (163 errors) and LobbyScreen.ts (107).

`npx vite build` alone (transpile only, no type check): SUCCEEDED in 2.43s. The main chunk index-*.js is 2,091.71 kB (579 kB gzip). There was one warning: '"LightningStrike" is not exported by three.module.js, imported by src/engine/renderable/fx/TeslaFx.ts'.

No dev server was started and no game assets were available, so runtime was not tested. The dist output was deleted afterwards.
feature_completeness:
"Code" means verified in this fork's code. "README" means a README claim only.
- Main menu (verified in HomeScreen.ts): the only active entries are 遭遇战 (Skirmish), Options, Info & Credits, a developer "底层测试入口" (low-level test entry) and Fullscreen. Quick Match, Custom Match and Replays are commented out. Mods shows the message "功能开发中" ("in development").
- Allied campaign: NO (code). No campaign or mission screens exist. A trigger engine exists (44 executors, 39 conditions in src/game/trigger), which is a foundation for missions only.
- Soviet campaign: NO (code).
- Yuri's Revenge content: NO for gameplay. EngineType.YurisRevenge exists, with theater and VFS mix lists (ra2md.mix, langmd.mix). SuperWeaponType has only RA2 entries (MultiMissile, IronCurtain, LightningStorm, ChronoSphere, ChronoWarp, ParaDrop, AmerParaDrop). There is no Psychic Dominator, Genetic Mutator, Force Shield or YR-specific units in the logic (code).
- Skirmish vs AI: PARTIAL. The skirmish screen, map selection and battle rendering exist (commits 0c5ea22 to 5b02f1d, 2025-09-13/14). The AI is effectively absent. loadBotsLib tries SystemJS '@chronodivide/sp-bots' and falls back to DummyBot.ts (53 lines), which only deploys its MCV and never builds or attacks (code). Upstream added a built-in bot later; this fork does not have it.
- Online/LAN multiplayer: NO. GameTurnManager is a no-op stub, WolConnection is a stub, and the menu entries are commented out (code). The README says "计划中" (planned).
- Units, buildings, superweapons: substantial RA2 logic is present. There are about 61 trait classes, including Garrison, Veteran, Temporal, MindController, Cloakable, Submergible, Transport, Harvester, GapGenerator, Parasiteable and Bridge, plus superweapon effects for Nuke, IronCurtain, LightningStorm, ChronoSphere and Paradrop (code). None of this was verified at runtime. TeslaFx will likely throw (see above).
- Naval units and water: logic exists (SubmergibleTrait, naval rules, ShipWakeTrailPlugin) (code). Water is rendered as original TMP tiles, with no water shader.
- Bridges: BridgeTrait and bridge overlay logic exist (code). Upstream later fixed bridge passability and render order, which suggests the snapshot's bridge support is buggy (inference).
- Garrisoning: GarrisonTrait and OccupyOrder exist (code).
- Veterancy: VeteranTrait exists (code). Upstream later fixed "veteran XP" (commit 924e97c), which suggests it is buggy in this snapshot (inference).
- Chronosphere, Iron Curtain, special abilities: effects and traits exist (code). Upstream later fixed the iron curtain effects.
- Fog and shroud: shroud yes (MapShroudLayer.ts, code). No fog-of-war system; RA2 by default has none either.
- Custom maps: MapFile parser and map selection exist. There are .map references, but no .mpr/.yrm handling was found (code). Maps also come from Chrono Divide's server URL.
- Sound, EVA, music: yes (src/engine/sound: Eva, Music, Mixer, WorldSound) (code).
- FMV cutscenes: NO. Only the menu video plays, and only as webm/mp4; .bik is unsupported (code).
- Save/load: NO. Zero matches for SaveGame/saveGame (code).
- Replays: a ReplayScreen/ReplaySel UI exists, but the menu entry is disabled (code). Not functional as shipped (inference).
- INI-driven modding: rules/art/ai/sound INIs are parsed into rules classes, and a mixin of mod INIs exists (GameLoader mixinRulesInis). Bundled overrides are in public/ini.mix and public/res/ra2cd.mix (code). The Mod manager UI is a stub.
- Map editor: NO (code).
- Performance at high resolution: not tested at runtime. Positives: batched and instanced meshes, a sprite batch layer, an octree frustum culler and VXL geometry caching (code). Negatives: the 2 MB main JS chunk and the stale WebGL1 instancing check (code).
Overall: a pre-alpha snapshot. Rendering and parsing are fairly complete. Gameplay is skirmish-only with no working AI.
asset_requirements:
VERIFIED in src/engine/gameRes (GameResImporter and related code):
- Required: ra2.mix, language.mix and multi.mix (requiredFiles). REQUIRED_MIX_SIZES pins retail sizes: ra2.mix 281,895,456; language.mix 53,116,040; multi.mix 25,856,283; theme.mix 76,862,662 (optional, music).
- Also used: the sidec01/sidec02(cd).mix side UI files, the theater mixes (isotemp/temperat/tem/snow/urban and so on), and audio.bag/idx inside the mixes. Yuri's Revenge mixes (ra2md.mix, langmd.mix, and so on) are referenced only if the YR engine type is chosen.
- How the user supplies them: at first run, through a browser file picker or the File System Access API (a folder, or loose .mix/.exe files, with the fsalib polyfill), or as an archive (.7z/.zip/.exe) unpacked in-browser by 7z-wasm. Files are copied into a browser-storage virtual file system and verified by size/checksum ("ra2.mix", ["E7BA3BE","5DC70844"]).
- The repo also bundles non-user assets: public/ini.mix (EA's rules.ini 541,915 bytes, art.ini, ai.ini, sound.ini, eva.ini, theme.ini, theater INIs), public/res/ra2cd.mix (Chrono Divide's own overrides and assets), public/general.csf, and Chrono Divide locale JSON.
- The default config.ini sets gameResArchiveUrl=https://download.ra2web.com/full-pack.7z and gameresBaseUrl=//wyhjres2.bun.sh.cn/. These are third-party hosts apparently serving the full retail game data (inference: likely unauthorized redistribution of EA assets; not downloaded or verified).
- For this project the user would need a legal RA2 copy (e.g., EA App/Steam "C&C Ultimate Collection" or original CDs) to provide the MIX files.
hd_extensibility:
Technically favorable. It is the same architecture as upstream and Chrono Divide, so this applies to whichever Chrono Divide-lineage base is used. It is legally blocked here. Where each upgrade would go, with rough difficulty:

1. Hi-res sprite replacement (units/infantry/buildings/anims; medium): src/engine/renderable/builder/ShpBuilder.ts (prepareTexture, useMaterial), ShpTextureAtlas.ts, BatchShpBuilder.ts, src/engine/gfx/material/PaletteBasicMaterial.ts and paletteShaderLib.ts (paletteColorFrag). Today textures hold palette indices and a LUT does the coloring. Add an RGBA path: a define such as USE_RGBA_MAP plus a house-color mask channel, so AI-upscaled RGBA frames at 2-4x resolution can be tinted by the remap color. Frames would be keyed by SHP name and frame number in an asset manifest, keeping the same world-space quad size and the anchors in src/engine/gfx/SpriteUtils.ts. The main work is producing thousands of consistent frames for every facing.

2. Terrain (medium-high): src/engine/renderable/entity/map/MapTileLayer.ts (createTileObjects), src/engine/gfx/drawable/TmpDrawable.ts and src/engine/gfx/TextureAtlas.ts. Swap the index atlas for an HD RGBA atlas per theater, keeping the per-tile vertexColorMult lighting. Cliffs and ramps (TMP extra data) and seams need care. Overlays and ore go through MapSpriteBatchLayer.ts and Overlay.ts.

3. Voxel upgrades (medium): VXL is already a real-time mesh (VxlGeometryMonotoneBuilder.ts → VxlGeometryPool.ts → VxlBatchedBuilder.ts/VxlNonBatchedBuilder.ts, lit by PaletteLambertMaterial/PalettePhongMaterial). Options: smooth the voxels (marching cubes or dual contouring plus normal smoothing) inside VxlGeometryPool; convert palette colors to albedo and move to MeshStandardMaterial (PBR) with house-color masks; or replace units with authored or AI-generated glTF meshes keyed by unit ID in VxlBuilderFactory.ts, preserving the HVA section transforms (turret/barrel).

4. Normal and depth-map lighting for 2.5D sprites (hard): sprites are unlit billboards (extraLight tint only). Each HD frame needs normal and depth maps plus a custom sprite shader that samples the scene's DirectionalLight and point lights. Depth maps would also fix sprite/voxel sorting and allow soft shadows. Lights live in src/engine/renderable/WorldScene.ts (ambientLight, directionalLight, updateShadowQuality), src/engine/Lighting.ts and src/engine/gfx/lighting/LightingDirector.ts.

5. Post-processing (medium): src/engine/gfx/Renderer.ts render() draws scenes straight to the canvas with NoToneMapping and LinearSRGB output. Render the WorldScene into a WebGLRenderTarget (HalfFloat), then run bloom, ACES/AgX tone mapping, color grading, SSAO (needs depth) and FXAA/TAA, then composite UiScene on top. Changing color management will change the palette look and needs retuning.

6. Water (medium-hard): there is no water shader. Water is TMP tiles plus tile animations (MapTileLayer anims) and ShipWakeTrailPlugin.ts. Build a mask of water cells from map tiles and LandType, render a separate shader plane (normal-mapped waves, reflection of the sky, depth-based shore foam, and wake and impact ripples fed from WarheadDetonateFxHandler.ts), and cut those tiles out of the atlas.

7. Weather (medium): add a scene layer in WorldScene for rain/snow/fog volumes plus a LightingFx subclass (the LightningStormFx.ts and NukeLightingFx.ts pattern) for storm lighting. The map theater (Theater.ts) can drive the defaults.

8. GPU particles and modern hit effects (medium): impacts come from src/engine/renderable/fx/handler/WarheadDetonateFxHandler.ts, which spawns SHP Anims (entity/Anim.ts, TransientAnim.ts). Hook there to add GPU particle bursts, debris, shockwaves, decals (Smudge.ts) and camera shake. Replace the dated global-THREE shader-particle-engine (used only in TrailerSmokeFx.ts) with a modern instanced or compute-based system. Fix TeslaFx.ts by importing LightningStrike from three/examples/jsm.

9. WebGPU (hard): all materials inject GLSL chunks into Three built-in materials. Moving to WebGPURenderer would mean rewriting paletteShaderLib and the Palette*Material classes in TSL. WebGL2 is adequate for this project.
Overall, the renderer is the most reusable part of the lineage for an HD remaster.
risks: LEGAL (blocking): the code is a reconstruction or AI decompilation of the proprietary, closed-source Chrono Divide client. The upstream author has formally stated (LICENSE, 2026-09-03) that the Chrono Divide-derived material is not licensed under GPL-3.0 or any open-source license. Building on it, and especially publishing or distributing it, infringes Alexandru Ciucă's copyright. The fork's stale GPL LICENSE file gives no real permission.

LEGAL: the repo redistributes EA-copyrighted game data (rules.ini, art.ini, ai.ini, sound.ini and others in public/ini.mix) and Chrono Divide's proprietary ra2cd.mix and locale text. Its default config points at third-party hosts (download.ra2web.com/full-pack.7z, wyhjres2.bun.sh.cn) that apparently serve full retail game files.

LEGAL/OPERATIONAL: config and servers point at Chrono Divide infrastructure (gameres.chronodivide.com, wol-*.chronodivide.com, and a CORS proxy on game.chronodivide.com), and the code tries to load '@chronodivide/sp-bots' at runtime, so it depends on a third party's servers without permission.
TAKEDOWN RISK: the upstream repo and its 252 forks exist only as long as the rights holder tolerates them. A DMCA notice could remove the base at any time.

STALE FORK: DD-Channel added no commits to main. It is 97 commits behind upstream (missing LAN multiplayer, the built-in AI, bridge, veterancy and iron curtain fixes, and performance work). The org bookmark-forks many unrelated repos.
INCOMPLETENESS: skirmish only, with a DummyBot that does nothing after deploying. No campaign, multiplayer, Yuri's Revenge gameplay, save/load, FMV or map editor.

CODE QUALITY: `npm run build` fails. There are 2,319 TypeScript errors once the dead file is excluded, 4,635 `any` usages, and strict mode is off. Minified single-letter variables and leftover SystemJS code remain. Dead builders use the removed THREE.BoxBufferGeometry. TeslaFx uses THREE.LightningStrike from three core, which does not exist (likely a runtime crash). The instancing capability check is stale (WebGL1).
DETERMINISM: the sim uses Three.js float math (src/game/math wraps three). Future lockstep multiplayer across browsers may desync (inference).
score_rationale:
Legality and licensing, weighted highest, score about 0. The code is admitted, and verified in the code itself, to be reconstructed or AI-decompiled from the proprietary Chrono Divide client, and the upstream author has revoked the GPL claim. It also ships EA and Chrono Divide data. A project the user wants to supervise and possibly show publicly cannot legally be built on it.

Completeness of original gameplay: about 2/10. It is skirmish-only with a do-nothing AI; there is no campaign, multiplayer, Yuri's Revenge or save/load.

Code quality and modifiability: about 3/10. The layout is sensible (sim, render and UI are split), but tsc fails with 2.3k errors, the code is heavily `any`-typed, and minified leftovers remain.

Renderer upgradability: about 7/10. Three.js r177 on WebGL2, a fixed orthographic 2.5D camera, a palette-LUT shader design that is easy to extend with an RGBA HD path, and voxels already built as real meshes.

Activity: about 0/10 for the fork. It is a dead snapshot 97 commits behind upstream, whose own activity is moderate.

Net: 1/10. The single point reflects renderer ideas worth studying, preferably in the upstream repo and without copying code. Recommendation: do not use DD-Channel/ra2-web or its upstream as the project base. Prefer a legally clean base (e.g., an actually open-licensed engine) or ask Chrono Divide's author for permission.
